# openobserve_anomaly_alert (Resource)

Manages an anomaly alert: a detector trained on a stream's history that flags each bucket whose value leaves the expected band `expected ± k·σ`, and notifies alert destinations.

**Requires OpenObserve Enterprise v1.1.0 or later.** Anomaly detection is not part of the open-source edition; against an open-source server this resource fails with a diagnostic saying so.

The series is one aggregation (`detection_function`) per `histogram_interval` bucket, read either through `filters` or through `custom_sql`. OpenObserve starts training as soon as an enabled alert is created, reading at least 21 days of history, and retrains every `retrain_interval_days`. Training fills `band_grouping`, `band_k` and the training span; refresh after training to see them.

The band is `expected ± k·σ`. Leave `band_width` unset to use the trained k (between 3 and 6), set it to fix k, or set `alert_budget_per_day` to let OpenObserve move k to hold a number of alerts per day. `band_width` and `alert_budget_per_day` cannot both be set. Changing `band_width`, `alert_direction` or the window settings takes effect on the next detection run without retraining.

Anomaly alerts live in **alert folders**, so `folder_id` refers to an `openobserve_folder` with `folder_type = "alerts"`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Anomaly alerts need OpenObserve Enterprise v1.1.0 or later.
# They live in alert folders, like every other kind of alert.
resource "openobserve_folder" "anomalies" {
  folder_type = "alerts"
  name        = "Anomalies"
}

# Request volume per 5-minute bucket for one service. The band width is left
# unset (Auto), so training picks k, between 3 and 6, from the data.
resource "openobserve_anomaly_alert" "checkout_volume" {
  folder_id   = openobserve_folder.anomalies.folder_id
  name        = "checkout_volume"
  description = "Unusual checkout request volume"
  stream_name = "app_logs"

  filters = [
    { field = "service", operator = "=", value = "checkout" },
  ]
  detection_function       = "count"
  histogram_interval       = "5m"
  schedule_interval        = "15m"
  detection_window_seconds = 3600

  alert_destinations = [openobserve_alert_destination.slack.name]
}

# p95 latency from custom SQL, with a fixed band and delivery settings: only a
# rise is delivered, and only once 3 of the last 4 buckets are out of band. It
# recovers when fewer than half of them are.
resource "openobserve_anomaly_alert" "checkout_latency" {
  folder_id   = openobserve_folder.anomalies.folder_id
  name        = "checkout_latency"
  stream_name = "app_logs"

  custom_sql = <<-SQL
    SELECT histogram(_timestamp, '5m') AS _timestamp,
           approx_percentile_cont(duration_ms, 0.95) AS value
    FROM "app_logs"
    WHERE service = 'checkout'
    GROUP BY _timestamp
  SQL

  # In custom SQL mode the field names the query's output column.
  detection_function       = "p95"
  detection_function_field = "value"
  histogram_interval       = "5m"
  schedule_interval        = "15m"
  detection_window_seconds = 3600
  training_window_days     = 28

  band_width               = 4 # expected ± 4σ
  alert_direction          = "above"
  alert_window_buckets     = 4
  alert_window_fire_pct    = 75
  alert_window_recover_pct = 50

  alert_destinations = [openobserve_alert_destination.slack.name]
  priority           = 2
  tags               = ["prod", "team:checkout"]
}

# Let OpenObserve move k to deliver about two alerts a day instead of fixing
# it. alert_budget_per_day cannot be combined with band_width.
resource "openobserve_anomaly_alert" "error_rate" {
  folder_id   = openobserve_folder.anomalies.folder_id
  name        = "checkout_error_rate"
  stream_name = "app_logs"

  custom_sql = <<-SQL
    SELECT histogram(_timestamp, '1h') AS _timestamp,
           CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN status >= 500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE) / COUNT(*) AS value
    FROM "app_logs"
    WHERE service = 'checkout'
    GROUP BY _timestamp
  SQL

  detection_function       = "avg"
  detection_function_field = "value"
  histogram_interval       = "1h"
  schedule_interval        = "1h"
  detection_window_seconds = 7200

  alert_budget_per_day = 2

  alert_destinations = [openobserve_alert_destination.slack.name]
}

# Filled in once training has run; refresh to see them.
output "checkout_volume_band" {
  value = {
    grouping = openobserve_anomaly_alert.checkout_volume.band_grouping
    k        = openobserve_anomaly_alert.checkout_volume.band_k
    status   = openobserve_anomaly_alert.checkout_volume.status
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `detection_function` (String) Aggregation computed per bucket: `count`, `avg`, `sum`, `min`, `max`, `p50`, `p95` or `p99`. Every function except `count` needs `detection_function_field`.
- `detection_window_seconds` (Number) Look-back of each detection run, in seconds. It must be at least `schedule_interval` plus `histogram_interval`.
- `histogram_interval` (String) Bucket width of the series, and so the detection interval, as a number and a unit: `30s`, `5m`, `1h` or `1d`.
- `name` (String) Anomaly alert name.
- `schedule_interval` (String) How often detection runs, in the same form as `histogram_interval`. It must be a whole multiple of `histogram_interval`.
- `stream_name` (String) Stream the detector reads. Changing it replaces the anomaly alert.

### Optional

- `alert_budget_per_day` (Number) Target number of delivered alerts per day. OpenObserve moves k to hold it. Must be greater than 0. Conflicts with `band_width`.
- `alert_destinations` (Set of String) Names of the alert destinations notified when the alert fires.
- `alert_direction` (String) Which excursions are delivered: `both`, `above` (value over the band) or `below`. Gates delivery only; detection still records both. Defaults to `both`.
- `alert_enabled` (Boolean) Whether detected anomalies are delivered to `alert_destinations`. Detection runs either way.
- `alert_window_buckets` (Number) Length of the alert window in buckets, at least 1. The window times `histogram_interval` must span at most 24 hours, which the server checks. Defaults to `1`.
- `alert_window_fire_pct` (Number) Percent of the window's buckets that must be out of band to fire, greater than 0 and at most 100. Defaults to `100`.
- `alert_window_recover_pct` (Number) Out-of-band percent of the window below which a fired alert recovers, greater than 0 and at most `alert_window_fire_pct`. Unset means equal to `alert_window_fire_pct`.
- `band_width` (Number) Band half-width k in standard deviations, between 1 and 10: the band is `expected ± band_width·σ`. Leave unset (Auto) to use the trained k, `band_k`. Changing it needs no retrain. Conflicts with `alert_budget_per_day`.
- `custom_sql` (String) SQL producing the series, for the custom SQL query mode. It must bucket with `histogram(_timestamp, '<histogram_interval>')` and return one numeric value per bucket. Conflicts with `filters`.
- `description` (String) What this anomaly alert watches.
- `detection_function_field` (String) Field the aggregation reads. With `filters` it is the stream field to aggregate; with `custom_sql` it is the query's output column that carries the value, for example `value`. Required for every `detection_function` except `count`, which it must not be set with.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the detector trains and runs. A disabled alert is neither trained nor evaluated.
- `filters` (Attributes List) Row filters, ANDed together, for the filters query mode. Omit both `filters` and `custom_sql` to aggregate every row of the stream. Conflicts with `custom_sql`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filters))
- `folder_id` (String) Alert folder holding this anomaly alert. Changing it moves the alert.
- `org_id` (String) Organization the anomaly alert belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `org_id`.
- `owner` (String) Email of the alert owner. Defaults to the account the provider authenticates as.
- `priority` (Number) Triage priority from 1 (most urgent) to 5. Display metadata only.
- `retrain_interval_days` (Number) Days between automatic retrains; `0` never retrains. Defaults to `7`.
- `stream_type` (String) Stream type: `logs`, `metrics`, or `traces`. Changing it replaces the anomaly alert.
- `tags` (Set of String) Selection tags, lowercase, for example `prod` or `team:checkout`.
- `training_window_days` (Number) Days of history training reads. Training always reads at least 21 days. Defaults to `28`.

### Read-Only

- `anomaly_id` (String) Server-assigned anomaly alert identifier.
- `band_grouping` (String) Slot grouping training chose: `weekend_hour` (weekday or weekend, by hour of day, from 3 or more days of data) or `global`. Alerts trained by older builds may report `hour_of_week` or `hour_of_day` until they retrain. Null until trained.
- `band_k` (Number) The model's k: the p99 training z-score, between 3 and 6, unless `alert_budget_per_day` has moved it. `band_width` overrides it when set. Null until trained.
- `id` (String) Resource ID in the format `{org_id}/{anomaly_id}`.
- `is_trained` (Boolean) Whether a trained model is in force.
- `status` (String) Lifecycle status: `waiting`, `training`, `ready`, `failed` or `disabled`.
- `training_data_end_us` (Number) End of the data the current model was trained on, in microseconds. Null until trained, and may be null in non-primary super-cluster regions.
- `training_data_start_us` (Number) Start of the data the current model was trained on, in microseconds. Null until trained, and may be null in non-primary super-cluster regions.

<a id="nestedatt--filters"></a>
### Nested Schema for `filters`

Required:

- `field` (String) Field to filter on.
- `operator` (String) Operator, for example `=`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `contains`, `not_contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `in`, `not_in`, `is_null`, `is_not_null`, `str_match`, `re_match` or `re_not_match`.
- `value` (String) Value to compare against, as a string. `in` and `not_in` take a comma-separated list. Ignored by `is_null` and `is_not_null`; use `""`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Anomaly alerts are imported as {org_id}/{anomaly_id}.
# The anomaly_id is in the alert's URL in the UI, or in GET /api/{org_id}/anomaly_detection.
terraform import openobserve_anomaly_alert.checkout_volume default/3LhlQwAIzEk7kGxqLOHIBgNiQtx
```
